question: A store offers three successive discounts of 20%, 10%, and 5% on a shirt. What is the single equivalent discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Multiplier = (1 − 0.20) × (1 − 0.10) × (1 − 0.05)

Net Multiplier = 0.8 × 0.9 × 0.95 = 0.684

Equivalent Discount % = (1 − 0.684) × 100 = 31.6%

**∴ Answer = 31.6%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three successive discounts: D₁ = 20%, D₂ = 10%, D₃ = 5%

**Formula used:**

Equivalent Discount for two discounts x and y = x + y − (x × y)/100

 Marked Price = 100 units -20% (20) -10% (8) -5/% (3.6) SP = 68.4 
• Total Discount = 20 + 8 + 3.6 = 31.6% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First two discounts (20% and 10%) = 20 + 10 − (20 × 10)/100

⇒ Equivalent of D₁ and D₂ = 30 − 2 = 28%

⇒ Final equivalent discount with D₃ (28% and 5%) = 28 + 5 − (28 × 5)/100

⇒ Net Discount = 33 − (140/100) = 33 − 1.4

⇒ Net Discount = 31.6%

**∴ The correct answer is 31.6% (Option 2).**
